[CC | 2026-06-22 — PROMPT 33 SHIPPED: timezone support, client-tz booking + viewer-tz display] — New day, new queue: Brayden had applied migrations 040+041 himself via the SQL editor (confirmed in LIVE_STATE — `db push` must NOT be run for those, applied outside migration tracking) and queued Prompts 27–33. Took the top of the queue, Prompt 33. **Recon:** confirmed `appointment_at`/`scheduled_at` were already `timestamptz` (correct UTC storage, migration 020) — step 2 of the spec was already satisfied, no fix needed. Found the actual bug: `CallModal.jsx`'s booking input used `new Date(datetimeLocalString).toISOString()`, which interprets the typed wall-clock time in the REP's OWN browser timezone — wrong when the rep is calling a lead in a different state than their own. Also found `AppointmentCard.jsx`'s reschedule input had a worse, pre-existing inconsistency: it displayed the initial value via `.toISOString().slice(0,16)` (always UTC) but saved via browser-local interpretation — two different timezone assumptions for the same field. **Built `src/lib/timezones.js`** (new, dependency-free): a 50-state IANA-zone lookup (`inferTimezoneFromState`, picks the majority-population zone per state — FL/IN/KY/etc. split states get one answer, matches the spec's "simple lookup is fine"), `zonedTimeToUtcIso` (interprets a datetime-local string as wall-clock time in an arbitrary zone → correct UTC, via the standard Intl.DateTimeFormat two-pass offset-correction technique — unit-tested against known summer/winter UTC offsets for Central and Eastern before committing, all correct), its inverse `utcIsoToZonedDatetimeLocal` (for pre-filling edit fields), `formatInTimezone` (display formatter), `timezoneLabel`/`SELECTABLE_TIMEZONES` for UI labels. **Migration 042** (`profiles.timezone text not null default 'America/Chicago'` — written, NOT yet applied, same SQL-editor pattern as 040/041, flagged in the file header). **CallModal.jsx (setter booking):** `appointmentAt` now interpreted/stored via `zonedTimeToUtcIso(appointmentAt, clientTz)` where `clientTz = inferTimezoneFromState(lead.state)` — the rep types what the prospect said, the system treats it as the client's local time, not the rep's. UI now labels the input "Appointment Time — Central (client's local time)" so the rep isn't guessing what zone they're entering. [CC | 2026-06-22 — Vault commit hit a stale `.git/HEAD.lock`, cleared safely + caught a concurrent Falcon commit] — While committing the Prompt 37 log entry above, `git commit` failed with "cannot lock ref 'HEAD': Unable to create 'HEAD.lock': File exists." Checked first (per the standing rule: investigate before deleting a lock file) — `ps aux | grep git` showed no running git process, and the lock file was 0 bytes, so it was stale rather than held by an active operation. Different from the already-logged `.git/index.lock`-under-OneDrive gotcha (that one is `Operation not permitted` on `rm -f`, unfixable from a sandboxed bash session) — this was a plain `HEAD.lock`, removable normally (`rm -f .git/HEAD.lock` succeeded immediately, no permission error). After clearing it, `git log` showed a NEW commit (`3c17d73`, "queue: Prompt 37 — tighten PASS 3 exclusion list") that hadn't been there at session start — Falcon's Cowork session had committed its local LIVE_STATE edits (the same Prompt-37 queue entry CC had already read off disk pre-commit) concurrently, which is almost certainly what caused the lock contention in the first place: two processes touching `.git/` on the same shared local clone at the same moment. Diffed the staged changes against the new HEAD before committing to confirm no silent conflict — clean, applied as expected — then committed as `6acad9f`. **Lesson:** a `HEAD.lock` (vs `index.lock`) with no running git process and 0 bytes is safe to remove directly; always check `ps`/file size first rather than assuming the OneDrive-permission variant. Also confirms Falcon (Cowork) and CC (CLI) really do share one local clone live, not just sequentially — concurrent commits are possible, not just concurrent edits.

## Session Log — 2026-06-26 (Prompt 119)

**No dashboard code changes this session.**

### Prompt 119 — Cowork mic stops after 1 second (Windows diagnostic)

Brayden reported: clicking the mic button in the Cowork tab records for ~1 second then auto-stops. Regular Chat tab mic works fine. Started after a hard GPU crash / unexpected restart. Already tried: full restarts, toggling VMP, enabling Windows Hypervisor Platform.

**Diagnostics run:**
- `CoworkVMService`: Running, Automatic — healthy.
- `vmms`: Not installed — expected. Cowork uses `vmcompute` (HCS) directly, which is running.
- Log location found: `C:\ProgramData\Claude\Logs\cowork-service.log` + `coworkd\user-*.log` (not under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Claude`).
- Searched 11,879 lines for audio keywords — **zero hits**. VM config has no virtual audio device (no virtio-snd). Audio capture is 100% host-side (Windows), sent to VM via RPC/HvSocket after capture.
- Event Viewer KP41: 4 crashes — today 3:38 PM, yesterday twice, 6/11. Recurring instability pattern.
- TDR (Event 4101): AMD GPU driver (`amduw23g`) stopped responding 6/20 and 6/15.

**Conclusion:** VM stack is a red herring — the 1-second cutoff is a host-side Windows audio capture failure. Most likely: MSIX app mic permission corruption from dirty shutdown, or stale WASAPI session lock.

**Recommended fixes (in order):**
1. Settings → Privacy → Microphone — toggle Claude off/on.
2. Settings → Apps → Claude → Advanced options → Reset (clears MSIX state, preserves VHD session data).
3. `Restart-Service -Name Audiosrv -Force` to clear stale WASAPI sessions.
4. If still broken: recurring KP41s (3 in 2 days) suggest RAM/PSU instability — run MemTest86.

## Session Log — 2026-07-04 (Prompt 213 shipped) — generalized say+fork combine; root-caused Objections two-click bug

**What happened:** Executed the queued [[LIVE_STATE]] Prompt 213 (two Practice-mode bugs Brayden caught reviewing Prompt 212 live — no matching entry in [[setter-script-v3-camden-style]] since this is a UI/routing fix, not a script-wording patch) in `ohvara-dashboard`, commit `6c054eb`, pushed.

- **Generalized the say+fork combine in `ScriptWalk.jsx`.** The old lookahead (Prompt 204/209) only checked ONE step ahead of a say for an adjacent fork — broke down for Pain's `do-the-math`+`reflection` (2 consecutive plain SAY lines before the fork) and Handoff's 3-line pitch, both needing an extra "Next" tap before reaching the actual decision point. Replaced with a chain scan (`sayChainForFork`) that walks all consecutive `type==='say'` steps forward and merges the WHOLE run onto one screen only if a fork immediately follows. `SayWithFork` generalized from a single `step` prop to a `says` array, rendering each line (with its own optional capture input) stacked in one screen before the fork options.
- **Scope question I raised and got resolved before building:** the doc's own wording ("chain together every consecutive plain-SAY step ... until you hit either a real fork OR THE END OF THE SCRIPT") read literally would also merge Vitals' 3 capture questions (ending in a route) and Close's 2-line outro (ending in an action) — neither flagged as broken, and merging Vitals specifically would've bundled 2 separate data-capture inputs onto one screen, changing the deliberate one-question-at-a-time pacing Vitals' own `tips` field calls for. Asked Brayden directly via AskUserQuestion; confirmed scope to fork-terminated chains only. Vitals/Close verified unaffected post-fix.
- **Root-caused the Objections "two-click" bug as a routing problem, not a fork-click problem.** Traced it live step by step: Objections' own "What's the objection?" fork actually resolves correctly in ONE click when reached directly (confirmed by entering the section directly AND by walking the real Handoff→Objections path) — the REAL bug is that Handoff's 4 non-"Picks a time" options all routed generically to the Objections section ENTRY POINT, which is that same "what's the objection?" fork — so a rep who told Handoff "just send me some info" then had to answer the identical question a second time before reaching `obj-send-info`'s actual line. Checked the source doc's own SECTION 4 spec, which always specified a DIRECT jump ("→ SECTION 5 (obj-send-info)"), not a re-ask — confirming this was a real implementation gap vs. the intended design, not a design ambiguity. Since this DSL has no cross-section sub-node routing (routes only jump to a section's entry, never to a specific node inside one), fixed by embedding each objection's actual response content directly under Handoff's corresponding option — same duplication pattern already established for every other convergent path in this file (qualifier, indeed-hook, etc. in Prompts 210-212).
- **Found and flagged, not silently fixed:** while tracing this, discovered the standalone Objections section's 5th branch, "Too busy / on a job," was ALREADY unreachable before this session — Handoff's fork never had a "Too busy" option to trigger it, a pre-existing content gap unrelated to Prompt 213's ask. Also asked Brayden directly (2nd AskUserQuestion this session) what to do with the now-doubly-redundant standalone Objections section object (4 of 5 branches now duplicated at Handoff) — confirmed to delete it entirely, including the orphaned "Too busy" content, rather than leave dead code sitting in the file. Removed the section plus the now-dead `routeTarget()` case for "objection."
- **Could not reproduce the reported green fork-coloring bug.** Tested the Objections fork's rendered button colors both via direct section-entry and via the real Handoff-routed path — both showed `rgb(239, 68, 68)` (red, `var(--danger)`), matching `CATEGORY_COLORS`' documented fallback-to-section-accent behavior for untagged routing forks, same as every other routing fork in the script (confirmed `--danger`/`--success` in `index.css`, no light-mode override exists to explain a color swap). Flagged this honestly in the commit/log rather than claim a fix for something I couldn't reproduce — also moot now regardless, since that intermediate screen no longer appears in the real call path after the routing fix.
- **Verified live** via the standing temporary `/dev-script-preview` route (removed pre-commit): Pain's 2-line chain + fork on one screen; Handoff's 3-line chain + fork on one screen; all 4 Handoff objection options (send-info, no-time, who-is-this, how-much) land in exactly one click on their real response text; Vitals confirmed still paced one question at a time, unaffected.
- `npx vite build` passes.

**Lesson:** when a bug report describes a symptom ("takes two clicks," "wrong color") but the stated root-cause guess doesn't hold up under direct testing, trace the ACTUAL interaction step by step (direct section-entry vs. the real routed path) before assuming the report is wrong OR patching the wrong layer — the real bug here was one hop upstream (Handoff's routing target) from where the doc's description pointed (Objections' own fork), and would have been invisible if I'd only inspected Objections in isolation.

## Session Log — 2026-07-05 (Prompt 218 shipped) — Handoff objection no longer re-enters Vitals; full route audit found no other instances

**What happened:** Executed the queued [[LIVE_STATE]] Prompt 218 (Brayden's live reproduction: Handoff's `"Who is this / what company?"` objection → `"That's me"` was landing back on Vitals' first question, appearing to restart the whole call) in `ohvara-dashboard`, commit `613b310`, pushed.

- **Root cause confirmed exactly as Brayden's hypothesis suspected.** `discoveryScript.js`'s Handoff section had `↳ IF That's me: → Go to Vitals Check` — a leftover route that was never repointed after Prompt 213's objection-embedding work moved this decision-maker check's logic around. `routeTarget()` matched "vitals" in the text and jumped straight to section 2, even though Vitals (and Pain, and the rest of Handoff) had already run earlier in the same call.
- **Full route audit, not just the one instance** (Brayden's explicit ask): grepped every `Go to `/`→ Go` line in the file — Opener(1)→Vitals(2)→Pain(3)→Handoff(4)→Close(5) is the section order. All other ~30 route lines are forward-only (Opener's qualifier fork → Vitals throughout, Pain → Handoff, Handoff's 4 clean paths → Close). **This was the single backward route in the entire script** — confirmed, not assumed, by checking every match.
- **Fix:** replaced the bad route with an inline embedded fork, mirroring the exact pattern Handoff already uses for its other 3 non-"Picks a time" objections (e.g. "How much does this cost?"'s "Just need a ballpark" branch): `"That's me"` → `"Does [Tuesday morning] or [Wednesday afternoon] work better for you?"` → `Picks a time [GOOD]` → Close, `Still hesitant [HESITANT]` → Follow-Up status (send info). `"That's [owner]"` gatekeeper-timing branch was untouched — it was already correct (forward to Follow-Up, no route at all).
- **Verified live** via a temporary `/dev-script-preview` route added to `App.jsx` (unauthenticated, mounts `ScriptWalk` directly with a demo lead) — walked the full Opener→Vitals(captured 3/day, $250 ticket)→Pain(engaged)→Handoff path, clicked the objection, clicked "That's me": now shows the new time-ask fork instead of re-entering Vitals; clicked "Picks a time" and confirmed it lands correctly on Close's "[Day] at [time]..." line. Route removed before commit — confirmed via `git diff --stat` that only `discoveryScript.js` changed.
- `npx vite build` passes.

**Lesson:** logged to [[Gotchas]] — `"Go to X"` routes in `discoveryScript.js` are just regex-matched section jumps (`routeTarget()` string-matches "vitals"/"pain"/"handoff"/"opener" in the route line's text), with no awareness of call history, so a route left over from an earlier version of the script can silently point backward into an already-completed section. Whenever a Handoff/Close-stage objection gets its content embedded (the established pattern since Prompt 213 for this DSL's no-cross-section-node-routing limitation), double check its resolution routes FORWARD, not to whatever the original standalone node used to route to.

## Session Log — 2026-07-06 (CC) — Prompt 239 shipped + pushed (`285ddc4`) — video anti-skip ceiling now tracks furthest-ever-reached

**What happened:** Built Prompt 239 from the queue. Root cause confirmed exactly as Eagle suspected: `video_positions` (Prompt 232E, `066_video_playback_positions.sql`) stored one bare number per video doing double duty as both resume-point and anti-skip-forward ceiling — `LockedVideoPlayer` seeded its ceiling (`maxTimeRef`) from `startAt`, and `exitVideo()` saved the *live* position at exit. So rewinding before exiting (or reopening into a rewound spot) permanently lowered the ceiling, forcing re-watching of already-earned ground.

**Fix:** reshaped each `video_positions` entry to `{ position, maxWatched }` in [TrainingCenter.jsx](../../ohvara-dashboard/src/pages/rep/TrainingCenter.jsx) — `position` still drives resume-on-reopen (unchanged), `maxWatched` is a high-water mark (only ever increases) that the anti-skip ceiling now seeds from instead. Added `getMaxWatched()` alongside the existing `getCurrentTime()` on `LockedVideoPlayer`'s ref so `exitVideo()` can save both values, taking `Math.max(prevMaxWatched, sessionMaxWatched, exitPosition)`. **No migration needed** — jsonb column, single consumer, legacy bare-number entries normalize to `{position: n, maxWatched: n}` on read via a new `normalizePositionEntry`/`normalizePositions` helper and get rewritten in the new shape on next save. Confirmed generic/per-rep by construction — keyed off each rep's own `training_progress` row, same as Prompt 232E, no hardcoded account.

`npx vite build` passes. Live-verified in the real Training Center (test rep, apex11): opened a video, played ~4s, exited — `localStorage.ohvara_training_video_positions` correctly wrote `{"1":{"position":23.66,"maxWatched":23.66}}` and persisted to Supabase; reopened the same video, resumed cleanly, no console errors across open → play → exit → reopen → exit. Could not automate an actual YouTube-iframe rewind/reseek (cross-origin, not reliably scriptable from outside) — verified the ceiling-seed change itself by code inspection (`maxTimeRef` now seeds from `Math.max(startAt, maxWatched)`; the existing "block scrubbing ahead" interval, unchanged, is the only thing that raises it further). Updated [[LIVE_STATE]] (moved 239 from queue to shipped). Prompts 240 and 241 remain queued.

**Resume prompt:**
`Read brain/Memories.md and brain/LIVE_STATE.md — continuing Ohvara work. Prompt 239 shipped + pushed (285ddc4). Next up: Prompt 240 (start-day star on shared RangeCalendar for Commissions + My Stats, plus verify it's generic/per-rep not apex11-specific) and Prompt 241 (My Payouts becomes range-aware, matching the 3 stat boxes; Last 30 Days chart stays fixed). Build top to bottom.`

## Session Log — 2026-07-06 (Eagle) — Decision: skip additional payout methods (PayPal etc.), existing bank flow already covers the edge case

**What happened:** Brayden asked whether PayPal could be added as a payout option alongside the existing Stripe-Connect bank-account flow, for the rare case a rep doesn't have a bank account. Researched PayPal's actual requirements (web search, current as of 2026-07): Payouts API needs a verified PayPal Business account PLUS separate PayPal approval for production access (review typically a few days, sometimes longer) — not a simple toggle. Flagged this as a real external prerequisite (same category as Twilio needing real credentials before those features shipped) and asked how he wanted to proceed. Brayden reconsidered: he doesn't want to chase ~5 separate payout-method integrations if each has its own onboarding/approval hassle, and asked directly what I'd recommend.

**Recommendation given (and Brayden's likely direction, pending his final confirmation next message):** skip adding PayPal or other payout rails. The actual underlying problem — a rep lacking a traditional bank account — is already solved by the existing Stripe Connect flow, since free neobank accounts (Chime, Cash App, Current, etc.) hand out real ACH routing + account numbers instantly with no credit check or minimum balance, and those work fine as a "bank account" in Stripe Connect today. So the edge case Brayden was worried about doesn't actually need a second payment rail — the fix is just "tell a rep without a bank to grab a free Chime/Cash App account," which costs nothing to build since it already works. Building out 5 separate payout integrations (each with its own business verification + ongoing compliance/reconciliation overhead) would be a lot of engineering effort for a problem that's already effectively covered. No CC prompt queued — this is a scope decision, not a build item.

**Resume prompt:**
`Read brain/Memories.md and brain/LIVE_STATE.md — continuing Ohvara work. So clicking Start Over silently added the old progress to the Back stack instead of clearing it — Back after Start Over popped right back to wherever you were. Fixed by having `restart()` call `setHistory([])` + `setState(...)` directly instead of going through `commit()`. This also means Back is now correctly *disabled* immediately after Start Over (empty history), not just visually reset.

## Session Log — 2026-07-16 (CC) — Prompt 288 shipped + pushed (`7e5f490`) — sidebar drawer, first Prompt 287 fix; found Brayden had already queued it as 288

**What happened:** Brayden said "run next task" after the Prompt 287 report — pulled the vault fresh and found Eagle had already queued the exact fix CC recommended, formally as **Prompt 288**, with a spec matching CC's own proposal almost line-for-line (md breakpoint, off-canvas drawer, hamburger toggle, close-on-nav-tap and backdrop-tap, conditional `ml-[240px]`, desktop pixel-identical). Built to that spec: `Sidebar.jsx` takes `open`/`onClose` props, uses `clsx` to combine `md:translate-x-0` (forces visible at `md`+ regardless of `open`, preserving desktop exactly) with a conditional `translate-x-0`/`-translate-x-full` (drawer state below `md`), a `rgba(0,0,0,0.5)` backdrop (`md:hidden`, click-to-close) rendered only when open, and `onClose` wired to both nav-link `onClick`s so navigating closes the drawer. `DashboardLayout.jsx` owns the `navOpen` state, auto-closes it via a `useEffect` keyed on `pathname` (so navigating away never leaves it stuck open), and renders a new mobile-only fixed top bar (52px, hamburger + "Ohvara" label, `md:hidden`) as the only way to open the drawer on mobile; `main`'s margin became `md:ml-[240px]` (0 below `md`) with `pt-[52px] md:pt-0` to clear the new top bar.

**Verification hit a real debugging detour worth logging as a pattern, not just a result:** the harness (`/qa-harness-287`, same disposable pattern as prior prompts) initially showed the drawer NOT opening after a hamburger click — `aside`'s `getBoundingClientRect().left` stayed at `-240` no matter what, even after full server restarts and fresh tabs. Root-caused via elimination: added a plain-text debug marker (`{navOpen ? 'OPEN' : 'CLOSED'}`) to bypass CSS entirely — it correctly flipped to OPEN, proving React state/props/clsx were all correct. Then checked the underlying Tailwind CSS custom property directly (`getComputedStyle(aside).getPropertyValue('--tw-translate-x')`) — also instantly correct (`0px`). Only the animated `transform` shorthand (driven by an inline `transition: transform 200ms ease`) stayed visually stuck at the old value. Tried `requestAnimationFrame` polling to let the transition settle — it never fired even once in 30 real seconds, which was the tell: **this headless/automated browser tab doesn't paint continuously between discrete tool calls**, so a CSS transition literally never gets the frames it needs to advance, no matter how much real wall-clock time passes between checks. Confirmed by setting `aside.style.transition = 'none'` — the moment the animation was removed, `transform` resolved instantly and correctly (`matrix(1,0,0,1,0,0)` open, `matrix(1,0,0,1,-240,0)` closed). **Lesson for future prompts:** if a harness check on an *animated/transitioned* CSS property looks stuck despite state being correct, don't assume the code is broken — check the underlying value driving the animation (a CSS custom property, a data attribute, whatever isn't itself transitioned) before concluding it's a real bug. A real user's browser paints continuously and never hits this; only this specific automated-tab environment does. Worth a [[Gotchas]] entry if this recurs.

**Full verification, once unblocked:** at 375px — closed by default (content width 135px→327px), hamburger opens (drawer slides to `left: 0`, backdrop appears at full viewport), backdrop click closes it again (confirmed via the debug marker flipping CLOSED). At 1280px desktop — sidebar `left: 0`, main `margin-left: 240px`, byte-identical to pre-fix, no hamburger/backdrop rendered. `npx vite build` clean throughout. Harness file and debug marker both deleted before commit — confirmed via `git status` that only `Sidebar.jsx`/`DashboardLayout.jsx` were in the final diff. Committed `7e5f490`, pushed to `master`.

**What's still open:** this fix alone doesn't make every page usable on phone — it just gives every page its screen back. The 5 per-page fixes from Prompt 287's audit (My Leads' fixed-width table, Script Walk/Call Now's fixed panels, AI Roleplay's oversized minWidths, Training's `minmax(240px,...)` grid, My Commissions' no-wrap KPI row) are all still unbuilt. ## Session Log — 2026-07-17 (CC) — Prompt 307 shipped + pushed (`385a8ee`) — My Leads padlock arch fused into body, centering confirmed already correct

**What happened:** Read [[LIVE_STATE]]'s "Next Up for CC" queue — Prompt 307 (4th round on this same lock shape: 300 → 301/302 → 306 → now) was the only fresh, non-blocked item; the other two open `🔲` entries (287, 270) are stale/blocked-on-signoff, not new queue items, so left untouched.

**Root cause:** `LockedVeil`'s shackle path (a stroked `<path>`, not a filled shape) ended both leg endpoints exactly at `LOCK_BODY.top` — the only overlap into the body was the stroke's own round end-cap radius (13px, half the 26px stroke width). That's a thin, imprecise junction, which is why Brayden's live screenshot still read the arch as "a separate piece sitting loosely on top" even after 306's square-body resize.

**Fix:** added `SHACKLE_OVERLAP = 60` in `src/pages/rep/MyLeads.jsx` and moved both leg endpoints down to `LOCK_BODY.top + 60` — well past the cap radius and the body's own `rx=20` corner curvature — so the union of shackle-stroke + body-rect is dominated by the body's straight edge right at the seam. No keyhole cutout existed (already replaced by the text/button region back in Prompt 302).

## Session Log — 2026-07-18 (Falcon) — Business-strategy pivot: multi-channel agent model, survey-as-script, staged team evolution — Prompt 309 queued

**What happened:** Long pure-conversation session (no code touched) working through a significant strategy pivot Brayden initiated unprompted, mid-way through an unrelated CC-queue session. Nothing was written down until the very end, once concrete decisions converged — see below for what's now captured vs. what's still just discussion.

**Core pivot: from "AI Receptionist is the universal pitch" to a diagnosed-problem model.** Brayden's original discomfort: the sales script assumes every lead's problem is missed calls, but Indeed (or other) signals might point to different pains. Resolution reached, in stages:

1. **Channel taxonomy (5 confirmed): Voice AI, SMS AI, Web AI, Email AI, Social Media AI.** Corrected from an earlier draft that flattened "universal categories" (Voice AI, Review Generation, SMS Marketing) together with "specific conditional jobs" (Dispatch, Quoting) — Brayden's fix: only channels (delivery mechanism) are top-level; everything else (review generation, lead follow-up, appointment reminders, billing reminders, dispatch, quoting, recruiting, etc.) is a *skill/job* that gets configured into one of the 5 channels, and several skills legitimately repeat across multiple channels (client picks which channel delivers that job). Full chart built and saved to the vault as `Ohvara_AI_Agent_Channel_Map.xlsx` (Voice/SMS/Web/Email/Social columns, italic-orange = repeats across channels).
2. **Fulfillment model: sell, don't build.** Brayden doesn't need the "two free testimonial builds" for HIS OWN confidence — the plan is to outsource actual builds (has a favorited list of Supabase-savvy agents on Upwork already, plans to get feasibility/cost quotes from them BEFORE outreach starts, so pricing margin can be sanity-checked against real build cost). Long-term end-state goal (not near-term): commission a meta-tool — "an agent that builds the agent" — an auto-provisioning system inside the dashboard that takes survey answers and auto-configures the actual client system, rather than a human manually building each deal. Sequencing agreed: build client #1 manually first (defines the template/spec), THEN commission the auto-builder off proven pattern + reinvested profit — not before. Confirmed this does NOT repeat the 2026-06-25 reverted "AI-generates-custom-stack-per-lead" decision (see [[North Star]]) — that correction was about the SALES/packaging layer (what to sell), this new idea is about the FULFILLMENT layer (how to build what's already decided) — different layer, not a repeat mistake.
3. **Survey architecture — adaptive/branching, not a flat form.** Per channel: broad non-presumptive gate question first, deeper quantifying follow-ups only if the gate confirms a pain (e.g. "are you missing calls?" → only if yes, "how many a day?"). Survey does NOT stop at the first hit — runs through all channels so multi-need leads get fully diagnosed. Target length 20-40 questions for the full/comprehensive survey variant (shorter, buildable-only variant discussed earlier in the parent conversation, not re-litigated this session).
4. **Pricing when multiple channels trigger: bundled, not stacked.** Highest-need channel priced at full formula value; additional triggered channels added at a reduced bundle rate, not their own full solo price (e.g. two $2,500/mo channels bundle to ~$3,500, not $5,000). Right-sizing principle: severity/dollar-impact score (each channel's own formula output) decides what's headlined as a front-runner vs. offered as a smaller optional add-on — so a business never gets oversold something that doesn't fit them yet, even if it'd technically help.
5. **Survey = the script, delivered two ways.** Not two separate tools — one shared branching question bank per channel, two front-ends: **live rep-driven** (dashboard shows the question, rep clicks the option based on what the prospect says — exactly the existing discoveryScript/ScriptWalk pattern, extended from Voice-AI-only to all 5 channels) and **self-serve async** (link sent like the existing rep-invite pattern, for inbound/inbound-ad flows with no live rep involved).
6. **Two distinct lead-gen channels, different survey delivery per channel — this resolved Brayden's own either/or question.** Outbound cold-calling (Indeed-sourced, warm-because-problem-aware) wants the LIVE variant — booking momentum lost if you hand off to an async link mid-call. Inbound (future, ad-driven, broad curiosity-hook creative — "if you're seeing this you're probably stuck on something...") wants the ASYNC variant since there's no live rep at first touch. Ad copy itself should stay pain-specific/narrow per variant (missed calls / slow quotes / no reviews / no website) even though the survey backend stays broad — direct-response ads convert on instant self-recognition, not broad appeal (car-ad analogy doesn't hold: "wanting a car" is a pre-existing desire, "wanting an AI agent" isn't — the wedge has to be the felt symptom, not the solution category).
7. **Setter's actual live-call job, once refined: find ONE confirmed pain (open, non-presumptive gate questions — not "do you miss calls, yes/no"), then book the meeting.** The FULL deep/quantifying survey happens live on the CLOSER's call (call 2), not the setter's call (call 1) — this is very close to the already-documented two-call sales process in [[North Star]] (rep gathers pain + books only, closer prices + pitches + closes), just made explicit that the setter deliberately stops at one pain rather than running the whole branching tree themselves. Resolves an earlier open concern (running 20-40 questions live on a cold first-touch call felt heavy) — now that length lives on the warmer, already-booked call instead.
8. **Three-stage team/comp evolution (Brayden's own framing, validated):** Stage 1 — appointment setters book, Nate closes (current documented process, mostly already built). Stage 2 — inbound ramps up in parallel with outbound, budget increases as it proves out. Stage 3 — once inbound flow is strong enough (survey pre-qualifies AND pre-books), setters convert into closers-only working purely warm inbound leads (5-6 calls/day, higher close rate, less grind) — appointment-setter role phases out. Commission-percentage-tracks-automation-value logic floated for Stage 3 (lower % than Nate's current 45%, since the system is doing more of the qualifying work a setter used to do) — **not built or finalized, current 10%/45%/45% + 50%/50% structure in [[North Star]] stays unchanged for now.** One open math question flagged: does the setter's 10% one-time cut fold into the Stage-3 closer's percentage, or into Brayden's — not resolved.

**Scoping decision for what actually gets built next: Stage 1, Voice AI ONLY.** Confirmed explicitly — the 5-channel/survey/bundling architecture above is a documented FUTURE-PHASE direction, not something to build now. Reasoning: Voice AI is the only channel with a working pricing formula, it's what the Indeed lead source already signals, and it matches the currently-locked North Star stack model exactly. The other 4 channels' pricing formulas, the bundling logic, and the full adaptive survey engine are explicitly OUT of scope until Voice AI's funnel is proven.

**Concrete build item queued: [[LIVE_STATE]] Prompt 309 — setter dashboard finalization.** Five sub-items: (a) rework the live script to be non-presumptive/pain-discovery-based instead of asserting "you're missing calls," gate-then-drill across multiple Voice-AI pain angles, setter stops at one confirmed pain then hands off to booking; (b) AI roleplay practice mode extending existing Retell roleplay infra so setters can rehearse the new script; (c) fix "video cards" — Brayden didn't specify the issue, CC needs to investigate and report back rather than guess; (d) settings tweaks — unscoped, flag back for specifics; (e) add-to-home-screen "Add Mobile App" install prompt (Android: real `beforeinstallprompt` intercept; iOS: instructional banner only, Apple blocks programmatic install) — approved to build now, not deferred.

**Not yet resolved / worth revisiting if this thread comes back up:** exact Stage-3 commission percentages and whether the setter's 10% folds into the closer's cut or Brayden's; whether the two originally-floated "free testimonial build" people still get approached (reframed as early qualified-demand leads rather than testimonials, per point 2 above, but not explicitly confirmed either way); pricing formulas for SMS/Web/Email/Social (deferred until Voice AI funnel is proven); real Indeed volume ceiling in the locked niches (affects when Stage 2 inbound stops being "someday").

## 2026-07-18 | Prompt 316 SHIPPED (`b04c6bd`, pushed) — turn-taking tuned, auto end-call wired, grading rubric rewritten, NOT deployed to Supabase (blocked)

**What happened:** Picked up the top item in LIVE_STATE's Next Up for CC queue — Brayden's real-call feedback on the newly-deployed v20 [[Prompt 315]] roleplay agent: (a) AI cuts him off mid-sentence, (b) AI never hangs up on its own, (c) `score-roleplay` grades a correctly-followed call poorly.

**(a) Turn-taking.** Retell's docs confirmed both `responsiveness` (how fast the agent starts responding after a pause) and `interruption_sensitivity` (how easily the agent's own turn gets cut off) were tuned too eager (0.7/0.8 in `create-roleplay-call/index.ts`'s `create-agent` call). Lowered both to 0.4 — the docs explicitly warn 0 disables interruption entirely, so didn't go that low.

**(b) Auto end-call.** Retell's `create-retell-llm` API supports a built-in `general_tools` entry of `type: 'end_call'` — Retell executes it server-side, no webhook needed on our end. Wired it into the LLM creation call and added rule 14 to the persona prompt: once the rep confirms the booked time back and gets the callback number, Mike says a short goodbye and the model invokes `end_call`.

**(c) Grading rubric — root cause found, matches the pattern flagged in the queue item.** `score-roleplay` is an LLM-judge (feeds a hardcoded prompt description to Claude), not keyword matching. That hardcoded description was frozen from before Prompts 309/312/315 reworked the live script — it told Claude the rep should "ask pain questions (missed calls, after-hours coverage, cost of a hire)," a 3-part probe. The real script asks ONE broad non-presumptive gate question and stops at the FIRST of 5 possible confirmed pain angles ("after-hours coverage" isn't even one of them). A rep following the real script correctly reads to the old rubric as under-asking — exactly Brayden's complaint. Rewrote the prompt's script description in `supabase/functions/score-roleplay/index.ts` to match the current 5-stage flow (Opener → Vitals → Pain Amplification → Handoff & Book → Close); the 5 score dimensions and 0-12 total are unchanged.

**Verified via two stubbed-Deno/fetch Node harnesses** (`node --experimental-strip-types`, temp scripts deleted before commit): confirmed `general_tools` carries `end_call`, `responsiveness`/`interruption_sensitivity` land at 0.4/0.4, every `{{var}}` placeholder in the persona prompt still has a matching `dynamicVariables` key (zero missing/unused), and the rewritten score-roleplay prompt renders correctly with a transcript interpolated. `npx vite build` clean — both are Deno edge functions, frontend unaffected.

## 2026-07-20 | Prompt 319 SHIPPED (`78c39b0`, pushed) — confirm-before-quantify gate on Vitals/Scheduling, roleplay NOT deployed

**What happened:** Picked up the top (and only) item in LIVE_STATE's Next Up for CC queue — a structural gap between Prompts 317/318 found by walking the real failure case: once an angle is confirmed at the opener gate (e.g. "calls piling up"), the script went straight to an open-ended number question and assumed a real answer would come back. A lead who picked an angle loosely at the broad gate could say "actually, we're not really missing calls" at the follow-up, and the script had no branch for that — it forced a number in (including a literal zero) straight into the pain-amplification dollar math.

**`discoveryScript.js` — new confirm gate on Vitals and Scheduling Check, Hiring Cost untouched.** Both sections restructured from a flat line list into a `BRANCH — Do they confirm?` right before their existing quantifying question: `vitals` now asks "So, are you actually missing calls?" and `scheduling` asks "So is scheduling actually the main headache?" before continuing into (respectively) the daily-miss number or the double-booking/wasted-time question. A "yes" leg is a verbatim pass-through to the unchanged existing content (same number questions, same captures, same downstream routing to Pain Amplification/Handoff). A "no" leg re-asks a short bounded 2-option reroute ("is it more the scheduling side, or you're just growing and need more hands?" from Vitals; the calls-vs-growing mirror from Scheduling) and routes into whichever of the other two sections (`Scheduling Check`/`Hiring Cost Check` from Vitals' no; `Vitals Check`/`Hiring Cost Check` from Scheduling's no) the lead actually confirms — plus a graceful Not Interested exit if the lead confirms neither, matching the established graceful-exit pattern used everywhere else in Opener/Handoff. Hiring Cost Check is untouched — it never asks the lead for a number (reflects `monthly_labor_cost` back as a statement), so there's nothing to gate. Wrote the two sections by hand rather than extracting a new shared generator function (unlike `painAngleBranchFlow`/`timeOfDayOfferFlow`) since only 2 sites needed this and their reroute options/phrasing genuinely differ (Vitals reroutes to Scheduling/Hiring, Scheduling reroutes to Calls/Hiring) — a shared generator would have been a premature abstraction for 2 non-identical call sites. Updated both sections' `goal`/`tips`/`trigger` fields to describe the new gate.

**Downstream matching pass — done, not deferred.** `create-roleplay-call`: `PAIN_ANGLES` entries gained `confirmGate` (true for the 3 calls-shaped angles + scheduling, false for hiring-cost) and `rerouteTo` (the OTHER angle indices each angle is allowed to reroute into, never back into the same bucket it denied — e.g. a calls-shaped angle reroutes to scheduling or hiring, never to another calls-shaped angle). New `CONFIRM_GATE_YES_VARIANTS`/`CONFIRM_GATE_DENY_VARIANTS` arrays, new rule 4c in the persona prompt, and the call-creation logic now computes `confirmGateResponse`/`rerouteResponse` — ~30% of eligible calls have Mike deny the gate and reroute, with `quantifyResponse` recomputed from the REROUTED angle (not the original) so pain/quantify can never mismatch across a mid-flow reroute, same invariant Prompt 317 established for the non-rerouted case. `score-roleplay`'s rubric (stage 3, Money Question) rewritten so a rep correctly re-asking after a "no" scores as good pain-discovery, not a missed beat — only dock points if the rep forces a number in anyway after a genuine denial.

**Verified — script flow:** a temp `buildScriptFlow()` harness (Node ESM, scratch copy with the one extensionless import fixed, both deleted before commit) confirmed all 8 sections reachable, all 3 terminal statuses reached, zero dead ends for 2 fake leads (with/without `monthly_labor_cost`), and specifically asserted Vitals' "No" branch has no direct route to Pain Amplification (grepped the file too — `→ Go to Pain Amplification` appears exactly once, inside the "Yes" leg only). ## 2026-07-20 | Prompt 320 SHIPPED (`4d212fe`, pushed) — mobile PWA persistent-login hardening + Supercell-style cold-launch splash

**What happened:** Picked up the next (and now only) item in LIVE_STATE's Next Up for CC queue. Two related mobile-installed-PWA-only asks, desktop explicitly out of scope.

**Item 1 (persistent login) — read the real code before touching anything, found no app-level bug.** Traced the full auth-restore path: `supabase.js` (client init) → `useAuth.jsx` (`getSession()` → `onAuthStateChange`) → `ProtectedRoute.jsx` (loading gate). All standard, correct Supabase-recommended patterns — no session-check race, no premature redirect. Researched the actual failure mode instead of guessing (WebSearch, 2 queries): iOS Safari has a well-documented behavior where installed home-screen web apps can have localStorage/IndexedDB cleared under storage pressure or long inactivity, independent of what the app does — multiple developer-forum reports (including iOS 17-specific regressions) describe exactly this "PWA requires re-login every time" symptom. This reads as the real root cause, not a code bug — but there's no way to be 100% certain without a real device. **Shipped the strongest available code-level mitigations, not a guaranteed fix:** `supabase.js` — made `persistSession`/`autoRefreshToken`/`storage: window.localStorage` explicit (was relying on implicit defaults) and added a `navigator.storage.persist()` request at boot (the standards-based signal that asks a browser to deprioritize this origin for storage eviction; Safari's own heuristics still decide, this doesn't force it). `useAuth.jsx` — added a standalone-mode-only cold-launch retry: if `getSession()` comes back empty on the very first check AND `isStandalone()` is true, wait 400ms and check once more before concluding "logged out" (guards a plausible race where an installed PWA's storage layer is still warming up a beat after JS starts running — a normal browser tab never hits this since its storage is already hot from the previous navigation). Explicitly did NOT claim this "fixes" the bug in the commit message or here — flagged clearly that it needs a real iOS/Android device test (fresh install → log in → force-quit → wait → reopen) to know how much it actually helped, since a genuine WebKit eviction decision can't be overridden from client JS no matter what.

**Item 2 (branded splash) — built, verified in a headless simulation.** New `src/components/SplashScreen.jsx`: full-screen `--bg-base` overlay, Ohvara logo fade+scale-in with a slight overshoot then a gentle pulse (`splashLogoIn`/`splashPulse` keyframes added to `index.css`), shown for 1.6s then fades out over 250ms. Gated in `App.jsx` via `isStandalone()` computed once through a lazy `useState` initializer — since React Router's client-side navigation never remounts `App`, this alone guarantees the splash shows exactly once per cold launch and never again on internal navigation, no extra bookkeeping needed. **Deliberate DESIGN.md deviation, flagged not hidden:** the Motion section caps everything at ≤200ms ("no duration > 200ms in the UI flow") — read that as scoped to repeated in-app UI transitions (hovers/tabs/panels), not a one-time pre-UI branding beat, since Brayden's own ask (explicitly Supercell/Clash-referenced, "a couple seconds") is flatly incompatible with a 200ms cap. Treated as an intentional one-time exception, not an oversight — said so plainly in both the commit and LIVE_STATE rather than silently overriding the design system.

**Verification — real, not hand-waved, but headless-only.** The Browser pane's screenshot action was timing out this session (environment issue, unrelated to the code) — worked around it with `javascript_tool` computed-style inspection instead of giving up on visual verification. Temporarily forced `isStandalone()` → `true` and `SplashScreen`'s `SHOW_MS` → 20000 (both clearly marked `TEMP-VERIFY-ONLY` in the diff while active), reloaded, and confirmed via `getComputedStyle` that the splash renders with exactly the right properties — `position: fixed`, `inset: 0`, `z-index: 9999`, `background-color: rgb(8, 8, 16)` (= `--bg-base`), both keyframe animations (`splashLogoIn, splashPulse`) actively running on the 96px logo — layered on top of the Login page underneath. Reverted both temporary changes immediately after, confirmed zero leftovers via `git diff`/`grep -rn TEMP-VERIFY`. Separately confirmed in a normal (non-standalone) tab load that the splash never renders (only Login's own unrelated `alt="Ohvara"` thumbnail present, count exactly 1) and the login form is immediately interactive — desktop/regular-mobile-browser behavior is unchanged. Also caught and fixed a subtle test-authoring mistake mid-verification: my first `querySelector('img[alt="Ohvara"]')` silently matched Login's own logo (same alt text) instead of the splash, giving a false "not found" read — switched to `querySelectorAll` + explicit computed-style comparison to disambiguate, a real lesson for future DOM-based verification in this codebase (multiple components reuse the same alt text). `npx vite build` clean, zero console errors in either mode. **What is NOT verified and cannot be from here:** whether the persistent-login mitigation actually keeps a real setter logged in after a genuine cold launch on a real installed iOS/Android app — that needs an actual device test, which the prompt's own verification section anticipated ("headless preview can't fully replicate PWA install/launch behavior").

## 2026-07-21 | Prompt 324 SHIPPED (`52917aa`, pushed) + deployed to Supabase — weekend lead-pause (opt-out default) + rep "Request Leads" escape valve, live-verified end-to-end

**What happened:** Picked up the top item in LIVE_STATE's Next Up for CC queue. Brayden's ask: reps shouldn't get a fresh batch on their own local Saturday/Sunday by default (give them the day off), but let a rep opt back in via Settings, and always give a manual "Request Leads" escape valve for a rep who wants to work the weekend anyway.

**Real gotcha found before writing any code — `useMyLeads` (`src/hooks/useLeads.js`) deliberately shows the rep's LATEST `batch_date`, not an exact match to "today"** (built that way in Prompt 195 to survive normal cron lag). Just skipping the cron on weekends would NOT produce "zero leads" — a rep who hadn't finished Friday's batch would keep seeing Friday's leftovers all weekend, the opposite of "day off". Resolved by making the frontend gate on two signals together: (1) is it currently the rep's own local Sat/Sun (`isWeekendInTimezone`, new helper in `src/lib/timezones.js`, mirrors the server's `isodow` check via `Intl.DateTimeFormat` so client and cron never disagree on what "the weekend" means) AND weekend_leads_enabled is off, AND (2) the most-recent batch loaded does NOT have today's UTC date (`rawLeads[0].batch_date !== todayUtcStr`) — i.e. it's a stale pre-weekend leftover, not something fresh. Only when both hold does `MyLeads.jsx` force `leads = []` and render the paused empty state; the instant a rep uses Request Leads, the RPC stamps `batch_date = current_date` on what it grabs, the date-match flips true on refetch, and the paused state clears itself automatically — no separate "unpause" bookkeeping needed. Verified this exact branching logic (4 real states: weekend+disabled+stale batch, weekend+enabled, weekend+disabled+fresh batch, weekday+stale) via a temp Node harness importing the real `isWeekendInTimezone` (`_tmp_verify_324.mjs`, deleted before commit) — all passed, including a cross-timezone boundary check (same UTC instant reads as Monday in New_York but still Sunday in Los_Angeles).

**Migration 071** (`supabase/migrations/071_weekend_leads_pause.sql`): `profiles.weekend_leads_enabled boolean not null default false`; `assign_daily_batches()` (016→064→here) gets one new `continue` right after the existing "already ran today" gate — skips on the rep's local Sat/Sun (`extract(isodow ...)` 6/7) unless opted in, and deliberately does NOT write `last_batch_assigned_local_date` on a weekend skip, so Monday's real run isn't gated by a stale "already ran" state. New `request_rep_leads(p_rep_id, p_count default 150)` RPC — adapts `request_closer_leads` (054/056) rather than building a second mechanism: same current-count-aware capacity math, but scoped to `assigned_rep_id`/today's `batch_date` (not an all-time total) against the 150 batch_size default, pool scope `assigned_rep_id IS NULL AND assigned_closer_id IS NULL AND status='New'`, grants `execute` to `authenticated`.

**Frontend:** `Switch.jsx` (new, `components/ui/`) — no boolean-toggle component existed anywhere in this app (only Button-as-toggle patterns like `Users.jsx`'s Activate/Deactivate), built a minimal pill switch on design tokens. Settings' `RegionalSection` gained a rep-only "Weekend leads" row (instant-toggle, no separate Save — a batch-pause preference should feel immediate, unlike the deliberately-considered timezone field next to it). `MyLeads.jsx`: `weekendPaused` state per above, a new empty-state branch (no lock, no training copy — explicit ask) with the message "No leads today — enjoy the weekend" + a **Request Leads** button (`useRequestRepLeads`, new hook in `useLeads.js`, mirrors the closer side's `useRequestLeads` in `CloserLeads.jsx`) that shows "+N leads assigned" or "No leads available in the pool right now" after clicking.

Applied cleanly to `jjextitmbptoaolacocs`, confirmed via `execute_sql` that the column and both functions exist.

Built all five statuses even though Follow-up and Not Interested have no data source today (calls happen on the agent's own phone, outside the app) — that was the explicit instruction, so the model needs no rework when live-call handling lands. `policies` carries the full Round 33 New Submission field list with `annual_premium` as a **generated column** (`monthly_premium * 12`), so it physically can't be hand-entered. RLS via a SECURITY DEFINER `can_view_agent()`: an agent reads their own book plus their downline's, admin reads everything, an agent only ever *writes* their own rows.

**`carriers` table ships EMPTY on purpose, and that's a deliberate design decision, not an omission.** Which carriers Nate/Jordan/Rego are appointed with is one of the three unanswered real-world inputs. Rather than seed invented carriers that look real, the Carrier Portals page gives admin an in-app add form — Brayden types the real ones once and they're live. Same reasoning applied to Quoter: it ships as a placeholder, not a fake embed.

**Six real pages under a new `/agent/*` tree** (closers land here on login now; `/closer/*` legacy routes deliberately left intact and still resolvable, per the anti-goal about not discarding old code): Overview, My Policies, Submissions, Carrier Portals, Hierarchy, plus Settings which already existed and is shared. Design details honored from the brief rather than reinvented: search moved onto My Policies instead of the global header (Round 32), status filters behind a Filters control instead of a permanent pill row (Round 32), detail popup is a **centered horizontal modal on `--bg-elevated` with background scroll-lock** (Rounds 36/37 — `--bg-elevated` is the modal surface in both modes per DESIGN v13, never the accent), sidebar regrouped into Sales / Tools / Growth (Round 38), coming-soon copy with no "before launch" (Round 37). The Effective-Date prompt ("Did this policy go into effect?" → In Effect / Undrafted) is real and stamps `effectuation_answered_at` so it never asks twice.

**⛔ BLOCKER hit, then cleared inside the same session (`65db56a`).** Initially: no Supabase MCP (confirmed via ToolSearch — earlier sessions had `apply_migration`/`execute_sql`, this one didn't), no DB password, v2 CLI couldn't see the legacy project link. Deliberately did NOT reach for `supabase db push` — prior migrations were applied by hand through the SQL editor, so the remote migration-history table is almost certainly empty and a push would try to replay 001–071 against a live database. Wrote a paste-ready handoff ([[claude-chrome-apply-migration-072]]) and reported the blocker. **Brayden then reconnected the Supabase MCP**, and 072 was applied directly with his explicit go-ahead (AskUserQuestion, "apply both" — matching this project's standing pattern that every schema change gets an explicit yes).

**Applied and verified properly, not fire-and-forget.** Pre-flight query first: confirmed both enums, `policies`, `carriers`, `upline_id` and all three helpers were absent (no collisions), `rep_invites` present (the policy swap had a target), `is_admin()` present (the new RLS resolves against it). Post-check confirmed every object landed, `annual_premium` is `is_generated = ALWAYS`, `status` defaults to `'Submitted'::policy_status`, RLS on for both tables, `rep_invites` now carrying the three new policies, and **zero rows disturbed** — no test data written to production at any point (deliberate: last session had to revert 150 leads after a verification click). `claim-invite` redeployed at **v5, ACTIVE, `verify_jwt: false`** — kept off because the signup page runs pre-auth and the invite token is itself the secret.

**Ran `get_advisors` immediately after, which caught two real self-inflicted problems — keep doing this after every DDL change.** (1) `touch_policies_updated_at` had a mutable `search_path` (the three SECURITY DEFINER helpers had it pinned; the trigger function was missed). (2) **`downline_of`/`upline_of` were callable by `anon` over `/rest/v1/rpc`** — given any profile UUID they return the IDs above/below it, so an unauthenticated caller could walk the whole agent hierarchy. Fixed in 073/074 after first grepping the frontend to confirm nothing calls them via RPC (`useHierarchy` reads `profiles` directly and builds the tree client-side).

**GOTCHA worth never repeating: `revoke execute ... from anon` on a fresh function is a NO-OP.** Postgres grants `EXECUTE` to `PUBLIC` by default on every newly created function, so revoking from a named role leaves the inherited `PUBLIC` grant intact — `has_function_privilege('anon', ...)` still returned `true` after 073. 074 revokes from `PUBLIC` first, then re-grants only where needed. **Caught only because the revoke was verified against `pg_proc` instead of assumed to have worked.** Critical detail on the re-grant: `can_view_agent` must keep its `authenticated` grant — it's called by the `policies_select` RLS predicate, and RLS predicates execute as the *querying* role, so revoking it would have locked every agent out of their own book. Final state verified: `can_view_agent` anon=false/authenticated=true, `downline_of` and `upline_of` anon=false/authenticated=false, `service_role`=true on all three.

**Pre-existing advisor warnings deliberately left alone** — ~25 findings against old-business functions (`assign_daily_batches`, `handle_new_user`, `resolve_login_email`, `process_lead_queues`, etc.) all carry the same mutable-search_path / anon-executable pattern, plus `pg_net` in public and leaked-password protection disabled. Not touched: that's a much larger surface and a separate decision, not something to fold into this prompt silently.

**Verification — honest split, and it's thin on purpose rather than overstated.** `npx vite build` clean. Dev server started, Login renders, **zero console errors**. Everything else sits behind Supabase auth and there is still no test login available — the exact gap Prompt 323 flagged after two reverts. Not claiming these pages work; claiming they compile and are wired correctly by construction. Someone has to sign in and click through before this is trusted.

**Deferred deliberately, all recorded in LIVE_STATE:** light/dark toggle (the live app has no light mode at all — no light tokens, no `data-theme`; DESIGN.md has the palette, wiring it is its own job), Underwriting + Stats polished-but-non-functional UI (Round 39 — pure UI with no backend, so it lost to the pages that needed wiring), and one honest security note: **Hierarchy's scoped visibility is enforced in the query, not in RLS**, because `profiles`' SELECT policy is `auth.uid() is not null` (migration 010, widened long ago so closers could read setter names). Fine for three trusted agents; must be tightened before this is resold to other agencies, and tightening it means re-checking every legacy page that joins `profiles`.

**Lesson:** when a prompt lists "real-world inputs that block parts of this build," the right move is to build the *shape* that accepts the real data (an admin-editable empty table) rather than either stubbing fake data or skipping the page. The empty state itself becomes the ask.

**Resume prompt:**

### 2026-07-25 (CC) — Prompt 334 shipped + pushed (`66af837`), all 12 carrier logos done, pending Brayden's screenshot verification

**Root-caused the cover-mode centering bug rather than guessing.** It wasn't `object-position` (already defaulted to center) — the real cause: the `<img>` is a flex item inside the banner's `display: flex` container, and a flex item's default `min-height: auto` is derived from its *intrinsic aspect ratio* for replaced elements. That let cover-mode images render taller than the fixed 84px banner and get cropped off-center instead of symmetrically. Fixed by pulling cover-mode images out of flex flow entirely — `position: absolute, inset: 0` on the image, plus `overflow: hidden` added to the banner div as a backstop — which sizes the image to exactly match the banner regardless of its own intrinsic dimensions. This is the standard robust pattern for `<img>`-based cover crops and sidesteps the flex/replaced-element quirk completely rather than patching around symptoms.

**Ethos** flipped to `logo_fit_mode = 'cover'`, no new image. **Transamerica** untouched, confirmed fine. **National Life Group** — took the fallback approach (crop, not re-source): wrote a quick Python/Pillow row-scan against the existing `national-life-group.png` (500×220) to find exactly where the tagline sat — logo mark spans rows 31–136, then a clean all-background gap from 137–157, then "Experience Life®" starts at row 158 with a hard edge (no anti-aliasing bleed into the gap). First attempt cropped to 167px and still caught 9 rows of the tagline's top edge — caught it by re-reading the cropped output image before shipping, not by trusting the math blind; re-cropped to 157px which lands exactly on the gap and fully excludes the tagline, verified visually a second time. Saved to `media/carrier-logos/national-life-group.png` in the vault, no external image sourced. Set to `cover`.

**Wired in Brayden's 5 newest real logos** (Corebridge, F&G, Fidelity Life, Foresters, Mutual of Omaha) — copied from `media/carrier-logos/` into `public/carrier-logos/`, deleted the old `corebridge.svg`/`foresters.svg`/`mutual-of-omaha.svg`/`f-and-g.png` placeholders (Fidelity Life had no logo before this — first one it's ever had), fit modes set per Falcon's staging notes (`cover` for Corebridge/Foresters/Mutual of Omaha, `contain` for F&G/Fidelity Life). ### 2026-07-25 (Falcon) — Prompt 335's "no bug" conclusion was wrong; found and fixed the real cause; corrected a flawed zoom_pct assumption; Prompt 337 queued

**Brayden's freshest screenshot proved the centering bug is still real** — Aflac and Chubb still visibly off after Prompt 335's harness check claimed no remaining bug. The harness confirmed the `<img>` box matched the container and `object-position` computed to 50/50, but never checked *where in the source image the visible crop window actually falls relative to the logo content* — a real gap in that verification method.

**Did that math properly this time, anchored to real numbers.** Measured the actual live banner dimensions directly off Brayden's screenshot (scanned pixel rows/columns for the Aflac card's teal color) — 325×82px, aspect ≈3.96. At that aspect, `cover` only shows the middle ~45% of an image's height, which massively amplifies small off-centeredness in the source file. Aflac's wordmark sits at 46.2% down its source image (small asymmetry in the full file) but that translates to a ~7px visible offset inside an 82px banner — enough to clearly read as "closer to the top." **Fixed at the source: re-cropped `aflac.png` (54px off the bottom) so the wordmark's top/bottom margins are now within 1px of each other** — staged in the vault, same filename, no DB change needed.

**Chubb's source asymmetry, by the same math, is only ~1px — should already be fine.** Left it alone and flagged it as a "if still visibly wrong after Aflac's fix ships, that's a real signal, dig deeper" item rather than guessing at another change.

**Foresters — Brayden re-sent the logo ("it got messed up") and it revealed a second real problem, plus a flaw in Prompt 335's fix for it.** The new image's own aspect ratio (1.74) is far more "square" than the banner's 3.96, so `cover` was cropping real content off the top and bottom of the logo, not just padding — matches his "barely fits, gets cut off" complaint. **Padded the new image with matching maroon background on the sides to bring its own aspect to ~4.1** (wider than the banner needs), so `cover` now only ever crops padding, never the logo — verified via the same pixel-margin check, symmetric to within a few px.

**Caught and corrected a real flaw in how Prompt 335 tried to fix Foresters (zoom_pct 85%) — worth remembering for any future case.** For a `cover`-mode image already absolutely-positioned to exactly fill its container, scaling it DOWN via `transform: scale()` doesn't reduce cropping — `object-fit: cover` has already determined the crop before the transform runs, so shrinking the result just reveals the banner's own background around the edges, defeating the whole point of `cover` mode (no white/background bleed). **The correct fix for "content getting cut off" is padding the source image's own aspect ratio, not scaling below 100%.** Zoom values above 100% remain valid (Corebridge's 110% is unaffected, F&G/Fidelity Life's 135% on `contain` mode is a different unaffected case). Reset Foresters' `logo_zoom_pct` back to 100 in the same prompt.

**One wrinkle Brayden noticed and asked about:** `app.ohvara.com` still loaded for him in his main browser (with a real dashboard, not an error) even though the GoDaddy CNAME is deleted and the domain is removed from the Vercel project. It did NOT load in a fresh Chrome browser he tried. Diagnosis: local browser-level caching (DNS resolver cache and/or HTTP disk cache) inside that one browser profile — Chromium-based browsers keep their own DNS cache independent of the OS resolver, and can also serve a previously-fetched page from disk cache without re-resolving. The fact a separate, never-used browser correctly failed to load it confirms this is NOT the domain actually still resolving publicly — infra-side it's genuinely gone. Told Brayden this isn't a production issue (new users/machines get nothing at that address) and gave him the fix if he wants it gone locally too: clear that browser's DNS host cache (Edge: `edge://net-internals/#dns` → Clear host cache) plus clear browsing data.

**Token-choice note, worth remembering**: `index.css` re-points `--text-primary`/`--text-secondary`/`--text-muted` to solid white specifically inside `aside` (`aside { ... } [data-theme="light"] aside { --text-primary:#FFFFFF; ... }`), which is why `--text-primary` was safe to reuse for a background fill here too, not just text color — it resolves to solid white in both light and dark mode *only inside the sidebar*, unlike the app-wide default. `DESIGN.md` documents a separate `--sidebar-text` token for this exact purpose, but it isn't actually defined anywhere in `index.css` — only `--sidebar-border` made it into real CSS — so using `--sidebar-text` would have silently broken (undefined var). Confirmed by reading the actual CSS before choosing which token to reuse, not just the DESIGN.md prose.

**Verified via computed styles, not a pixel screenshot** — same Browser-pane-not-displayed situation as the Prompt 340 session (`computer{screenshot}` timed out). ### 2026-07-26 (CC) — Prompt 349 shipped: attention-feed clipping root-caused and fixed, badges recolored

Picked up Prompt 349 (found queued below the just-shipped Prompt 350, out of numeric order in the doc but still genuinely next). This one paid off measuring the real DOM instead of guessing from the CSS — the actual root cause wasn't what a code read alone would have suggested.

**What happened:** Discovered — using a real persisted browser session that could hit `/agent` directly, no harness needed this time — that the "Needs your attention" card's Name/Detail columns are only ~76px/~137px wide at a common 1280px viewport (the card splits 50/50 with "Monthly goal"), narrow enough that Prompt 347's `minHeight: 42` (only ever a floor) let almost any real name/detail wrap to 2 lines, measuring rows at **63.5px** live — well past the container's hardcoded `42 * 5 = 210px` cap. That's the exact "clips mid-row" bug from Brayden's screenshot, and it wasn't a border-rounding or padding-math issue like the CSS alone might have suggested — it was text wrapping in an undersized column. Fixed in `AgentOverview.jsx` by switching to a real fixed `height` (not `minHeight`) plus a new `ATTENTION_CLIP` style (ellipsis truncation + `minWidth: 0`, needed because CSS Grid items don't shrink below their content's intrinsic width by default) on the Name/Detail spans. Also added a `--purple` token to `index.css` (dark `#A855F7` / light `#5B21B6`, matching the existing success/warning/danger/info base+dim+bd pattern — no purple token existed before) and recolored Confirm Effective to it; recolored Follow-up to `var(--info)` after confirming via `MyCalls.jsx` that My Calls → Schedule's own FOLLOW-UP badge already uses that exact token, so this is a literal match, not just "some blue."

**Real finding flagged, not silently absorbed:** fixing the height bug surfaces a genuine side-effect — forcing single-line-only means names now visibly truncate with an ellipsis far more often than not at ~1280-1366px screens (measured: every one of the 7 seeded rows' Name spans truncating at 1280px). This isn't new information exactly — the same narrow columns existed before, they just wrapped instead of truncating (readable, if tall) — but it's a real visible tradeoff worth Brayden knowing about rather than discovering in his next screenshot review. Fixing it properly would mean widening the card (e.g. dropping the strict 50/50 split with Monthly goal), which is a bigger layout call than this prompt asked for, so flagged in LIVE_STATE rather than built unilaterally.

**Verified via real DOM measurement**, not just a rendered page: `getBoundingClientRect().height` on all 7 real attention rows went from 63.5/63.5/63.5/63.5/63.5/63.5/62.5 (before) to a flat 42/42/42/42/42/42/42 (after) — `scrollHeight` 294 = 42×7 exactly, container `clientHeight` 210 = 42×5 exactly, zero partial-row overflow. Computed `color` on each tag pill confirmed the exact expected RGB for all three badge colors. Browser-pane screenshot hit the same known compositing timeout as recent prompts — substituted DOM measurement again, same established pattern. `npx vite build` clean.

### 2026-07-26 (CC) — Prompt 353 shipped: clock baseline/sizing bugs root-caused to Playfair Display's default old-style figures, fixed with `lining-nums`

Picked up Prompt 353, next after 354 — real rendering bugs Brayden found living with Prompt 350's font swap (digits dipping below AM/PM's baseline, digits looking inconsistently sized), not a new redesign. The prompt's own hypothesis for bug 1 was a `vertical-align`/`line-height` issue from the digits/AM-PM span split — that hypothesis was wrong, and proving it wrong (rather than patching layout blindly) is what actually found the fix.

**What happened, and how the real root cause was found:** used `canvas.measureText().actualBoundingBoxAscent/actualBoundingBoxDescent` (true glyph-ink metrics, not CSS box metrics) on each digit 0-9 in Playfair Display 700. Found `3/4/5/7/9` have a real 5px descent below the baseline, `6/8` have a 22px ascent (cap-height, vs 16px for `0/1/2`), and glyph widths vary despite `tabular-nums` — the textbook signature of **old-style (text) figures**, which is Playfair Display's default numeral style. That's Brayden's "3 extends below AM's baseline" bug AND the "digits look inconsistent size" bug from one single cause, not two bugs and not a vertical-align/line-height issue at all — the digits/AM-PM span split from Prompt 350 was never the problem. Fix: added `lining-nums` to the existing `fontVariantNumeric` in `AgentOverview.jsx` (now `CLOCK_NUMERIC_VARIANT = 'lining-nums tabular-nums'`), switching to the font's lining-figure glyphs (uniform height, sit on baseline, no ascenders/descenders) while keeping digits fixed-width for the ticking clock. Bumped digit size 30px → 36px (`CLOCK_DIGIT_SIZE`) now that glyphs are actually uniform; AM/PM is now computed as `CLOCK_DIGIT_SIZE / 2` instead of a second hardcoded number, so the "exactly half" rule can't drift out of sync in a future prompt.

**Verified with real pixel-ink measurement**, the most rigorous check run on this project so far: canvas taint rules block the obvious approach (rasterizing an SVG `foreignObject` — Chromium always taints that for canvas regardless of origin), so built a same-origin-safe rasterizer instead: fetched the actual served Playfair Display 700 woff2, embedded it as a base64 data URI inside a pure-SVG `<text>` element (no `foreignObject`), drew it to canvas, and scanned real pixel alpha for each glyph's true ink top/bottom. Confirmed empirically — not assumed — that `font-variant-numeric` only takes effect via the SVG `style` attribute (CSS), not the raw XML presentation attribute (a real gotcha, logged separately if it recurs). Results: **before** (`tabular-nums` only) `3`/`9` measured baseline+8 to baseline-32 (40px, descending) and `6`/`8` measured baseline+0 to baseline-44 (44px, ascending) — provably different footprints. **After** (`lining-nums tabular-nums`) `0/3/6/9` all measured identically at baseline+0 to baseline-26 (26px) at the real 36px digit size, and `A/M/P` at the real 18px AM/PM size measured baseline-1 to baseline-13 — digits and AM/PM now share the same baseline with nothing dipping below it. Cross-checked against the real component via a disposable `QaHarness353.jsx` (mocked `AuthContext` + pre-seeded react-query cache, same established pattern): live-rendered clock computed to `fontSize: 36px`, `fontVariantNumeric: "lining-nums tabular-nums"`, AM/PM span `fontSize: 18px` — confirms the fix lands correctly in situ, not just in the isolated rasterizer test. Browser-pane screenshot hit the same known compositing timeout as recent prompts — substituted, same established pattern. Harness + temp route + temp `AuthContext` export fully reverted before commit (`git status` showed only the 1 real file changed). `npx vite build` clean.

**Queue still has 2 items** (352 drop Persistency's period picker, 351 My Policies inline effectuation confirm).

Picked up Prompt 351, the last item in the queue — builds on Prompt 345's effectuation Yes/No (moved from a page banner onto the record). Real problem: no way to find which policy needed confirming without searching/scrolling. Three parts, all landed in `MyPolicies.jsx`.

**What happened:** (1) `rows` now computes `pendingIds` from the existing `pendingEffectuation()` helper (reused from Prompt 345, not duplicated) and does a stable sort so awaiting-confirmation rows lead, everything else keeps `usePolicies`' existing order behind them. (2) A pending row renders as two `<tr>`s in a `Fragment` — first line is the normal columns with `borderBottom: 'none'` on every cell (no divider), second is a `colSpan={7}` warning-styled banner (`Bell` icon, the same "did this policy go into effect?" copy + Yes/No buttons calling the same `answerEffectuation()`/`useUpdatePolicy()` mutation PolicyModal's own banner uses) that supplies the row's real outer border — the two `<tr>`s read as one fused two-line box. PolicyModal's own Yes/No is untouched, this just adds a faster path. (3) New `carrierPortalUrl(policy)` matches `useCarriers()` data on `carrier_id` first, `carrier_name` as fallback, rendering "Not sure? Check {carrier} portal" as a new-tab link, or a muted "no portal on file" message when the carrier has none — same disabled-state convention as Carrier Portals' own cards. Scope respected: only effectuation-pending rows get this treatment, cancellation-pending and other states untouched.

**Found and fixed a real harness bug in the process, not just the feature — worth its own Gotchas entry ([[Gotchas]]), not just buried here:** the first QA pass showed BOTH pending test rows as "no portal on file," including the one whose fake carrier had a `portal_url` set. Root-caused via `queryClient.getQueryState(['carriers'])` (exposed the QueryClient on `window` temporarily for debugging, removed before revert): `dataUpdateCount: 2`, `status: "success"`, `data: []`. Unlike `usePolicies` (whose fake `agent_id: 'qa-agent'` trips a Postgres `22P02` invalid-uuid-cast error and leaves the pre-seeded cache alone — `fetchFailureCount: 1`, data unchanged), `useCarriers()`'s plain `select('*')` has no filter to fail on, so it fired a real anon-key read against the actual production `carriers` table on mount and silently overwrote the seed with an empty result — `useQuery` defaults to `refetchOnMount: true`/`staleTime: 0` regardless of pre-seeded data. **This means every prior harness (348/350/353/354) was only accidentally safe** — protected by their fake filters happening to error, not by any real safeguard. Fixed by giving this harness's `QueryClient` explicit `{ retry: false, refetchOnMount: false, refetchOnWindowFocus: false, staleTime: Infinity }` defaults, which is now the recommended default for every future harness, not just when a mismatch is visibly wrong.

**Verified via disposable `QaHarness351.jsx`** (real login blocked by the auto-mode classifier again, same fallback as Prompt 352): seeded 4 fake policies (2 pending on different carriers — one with a portal on file, one without — plus 1 `In Effect` and 1 future-dated `Submitted`) in deliberately non-sorted order. After the QueryClient fix: `read_page`/`get_page_text` confirmed both pending rows sorted to the top in their original relative order (proving the sort is genuinely stable, not coincidental), Bob Baker/Foresters correctly showed "No portal on file," Alice Anderson/Mutual of Omaha correctly showed the link with `href="https://portal.example.com/moo"`. Computed styles on the `<tr>`s confirmed the fused-box structure (`borderBottomStyle: 'none'` on the first line's cells, `'solid'` + `colSpan: 7` on the banner line). Clicked into the full record and confirmed PolicyModal's own Prompt-345 banner still renders unchanged — both paths work, as the prompt's verify criteria asked. Screenshot hit the same known Browser-pane compositing timeout as every recent prompt — substituted, same established pattern. Harness, temp `/qa351` route, and temp `AuthContext` export fully reverted before commit (`git status` showed only the 1 real file changed). `npx vite build` clean both before and after revert.

## 2026-07-26 (CC) — Prompt 360 shipped (`ae3939b`, pushed) — clock jitter root-caused to a font limitation, attention columns rebalanced

Both fixes verified via isolated harness (no login credentials available for the live dashboard from this CLI session — same limitation as [[Gotchas]]'s rep-auth-gated visual-check entry) rather than a real screenshot; both are static-layout/CSS fixes with no runtime data dependency, so the harness result should transfer directly, but Brayden's normal screenshot verification still applies before fully trusting it.

- **Clock jitter root cause found, and it wasn't what Prompt 353 assumed.** `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` has been on the clock since Prompt 353, yet the pill kept visibly resizing every second. Copied the actual self-hosted `@fontsource/playfair-display` woff2 into an isolated test harness and measured real `getBoundingClientRect()` widths per digit at 36px/700 — `tabular-nums` applied vs. omitted produced *identical* widths (14.0px–23.5px spread either way). Playfair Display simply has no `tnum` OpenType feature table entry, so the CSS property is silently accepted and does nothing — confirming the task's own hunch ("check if Playfair Display actually supports a tabular figure variant, since not all fonts do"). `lining-nums` (the baseline/ascender fix from Prompt 353) is real and stays; `tabular-nums` is dropped since it was dead weight.
- **Fix: CSS-level fixed-width digit wrapper, not a font-feature.** Since the font can't be trusted to do this itself, each `0-9` character in the clock string is now wrapped in its own `display:inline-block; width:0.68em` span (`renderClockDigits()` in `AgentOverview.jsx`); colons pass through unwrapped since they never change value. Re-verified in the same harness: total rendered string width was identical (147.781px, to 3 decimal places) across 8 different digit combinations (00:00–99:99-style), vs. real jitter without the wrapper.
- **"Needs your attention" columns: the `1fr`/`1.8fr` tracks were already using the full box width — the bug was the fixed `150px` Type column.** Measured the real grid math both by hand and in a harness at the actual ~810px card width: Name/Detail were already stretching correctly as the card widened (that part of Prompt 354 worked as intended). The visible "clumped left, dead space on the right" was the Type column reserving a flat 150px for a pill that only ever renders ~55–80px wide — 70–95px of permanent dead space on every row, invisible to the fr-based math but real on screen. Changed Type to `minmax(70px,max-content)` (shrinks to the pill's real content) and bumped the shared column gap 12→20, letting the reclaimed width flow into Name/Detail automatically. Verified in-harness: Type 150px→~57-79px, Name 192px→~230px, Detail 346px→~368px, row content now reaches to within ~1px of the card's right padding edge (previously stopped ~24px short). Header and data rows now share one `ATTENTION_COLUMNS` constant so they can't drift apart.
- Lint (`eslint`) and `vite build` both clean. Prompt 361 (AccountMenu sign-out → red) is next in queue, added by Falcon mid-session.
