## 2026-07-29 (CC) — Prompt 387 shipped (`b626f7b`, pushed) — New Submission's State dropdown now always opens downward

**Root cause: this is a native-`<select>` limitation, not a CSS bug.** A native `<select>`'s popup open-direction is chosen entirely by the browser, and the heuristic isn't a strict "is there room below the trigger" check — it's closer to "which half of the viewport is the trigger in." Confirmed via harness measurement at a 720px-tall viewport: Insurance Provider (row 2 of 5, `y: 225`, 462px of room below) stayed comfortably in the upper half; State (row 4 of 5, `y: 357`, only 330px below, past the viewport midpoint) is exactly the field Brayden's screenshot showed flipping upward — matches the theory precisely. There is no CSS property that overrides a native select's popup direction, so the only real fix is to stop using a native select for this field.

- **New `AnchoredSelectField` component** in `ExportForm.jsx` — a from-scratch dropdown (button trigger + absolutely-positioned option list, `position: 'absolute', top: '100%'`, click-outside-to-close) styled to match `SelectField`'s existing look exactly (`control`/`fieldLabel` tokens, no new visual language). Since it's real DOM in normal page flow rather than an OS-rendered popup, it always opens below its own trigger — no viewport-heuristic to fight.
- Swapped only the **State** field in `Submissions.jsx`'s New Submission form to use it. Left Insurance Provider and Product Type as native `SelectField`s — per the prompt's own scope ("check... confirm they don't have the same issue," not "fix them too") — and the harness measurement above confirms they don't: both sit well above the viewport's vertical midpoint at any realistic screen height, so they weren't going to flip. Did **not** touch the shared `SelectField` component or any of its other ~10+ usages across the app (Settings, other forms, the underwriting-decision field on this same form) — this is scoped to the one field that actually broke, not a wholesale native-select replacement.
- **Verified via the same isolated-harness pattern as Prompts 386/385** (mocked `AuthContext` + seeded `['carriers']`/`['commission-schedule']`/`['policies','visible']` query data, real `Submissions` component rendered at a 720px viewport). Measured both the trigger's `getBoundingClientRect()` and the opened list's position directly: list top (395px) sits ~4px below the button's bottom edge (391px) — `opensBelow: true`. Also drove a real selection through the DOM (clicked "California") and confirmed the trigger's label updated to "California," proving the value/onChange wiring works end-to-end, not just the visual open direction. Harness route and the temporary `AuthContext` export were both reverted before commit.
- `eslint`/`vite build` both clean, no pre-existing errors touched.

## 2026-07-29 (CC) — Prompt 384: migration 090 written and pushed (`fa8c38f`) — 4 of 9 trigger types built, 1 flagged as unbuildable without a design call, 2 already real, live-DB steps blocked on Brayden

**Built for real (migration `090_real_notification_triggers.sql`, all following [[Prompt 357]]'s migration-084 `security definer` trigger pattern so inserts bypass RLS regardless of who/what caused them):**

Confirmed via investigation that `profiles` rows are created by the existing `handle_new_user()` trigger on `auth.users` insert (migration 005) via `claim-invite`'s `admin.createUser()` call — trigger chaining means my new AFTER INSERT trigger on `profiles` fires automatically from that same insert, no changes needed to `claim-invite` itself.

Added a new `lapse_check_notified_at` column + a `before update` trigger that clears it whenever `next_lapse_check_at` changes (so the *next* occurrence gets its own notification, not just the first) + a daily `pg_cron` job (`notify-lapse-checkins`, 6:05am UTC — pg_cron/pg_net were already enabled and in active use elsewhere in this codebase, migration 002, so this isn't new infrastructure) that atomically finds due, not-yet-notified policies and inserts+stamps in one CTE statement to avoid a read/write race.

- Made AnchoredSelectField's label paragraph conditional so it can drop into inline rows that already carry their own external label (Settings, Payouts, CallModal) without leaving an empty label gap - small addition to the shared component, not a new one.
- Real bug caught before it shipped: a naive conversion using placeholder text like "All carriers" instead of a real value/label option would have made the "reset to All" filter state unreachable - AnchoredSelectField's placeholder is button text shown only when nothing matches, not a selectable row in the open panel. Fixed by keeping the blank/"All ___" choice as a genuine first option everywhere it's a real re-selectable filter state (My Policies filters, Compensation Grid filters, PolicyModal's "Not started" cancellation status) - only used bare placeholder text where the blank state is a one-time initial pick that's never revisited (Submissions' Insurance provider/Product type, Payouts' rep picker), matching the existing State-field convention from Prompt 387.

Gotcha worth remembering: pages/agent/CompensationGrid.jsx has a literal stray null byte instead of a space in its products map-key line (between the carrier and product template interpolations) - pre-existing, confirmed via git diff showing no textual change touched that line. It silently makes ripgrep/Grep treat the whole file as binary and skip pattern matches with zero warning (cost real time this session - the file's two selects didn't show up in the first pass of greps, only surfaced via reading the file directly and later a forced-text grep pass). Harmless functionally (the odd key still works as a Map key), flagged as a separate spawned task rather than fixed inline to keep this PR scoped to the dropdown work. Lesson: when auditing a codebase with Grep and a file that should obviously match doesn't, try reading it directly or forcing text mode - don't trust a clean "no matches" from a tool that silently skips files it thinks are binary.

Key realization while implementing: Approval Rate was a flow metric (submitted-in-period denominator), but the given formula for Early Cancellation Rate has no period/window term at all - it's a ratio over the whole book as of a date, so it actually belongs on the snapshot side (same shape as its row-neighbor Fall-off Rate), not the flow side. Added earlyCancellationRate to productionSnapshot(): denominator = policies with status='In Effect' OR any cancellation_status (as of the snapshot date); numerator = of those, cancellation_status set AND cancellation_call_at within 30 days of effective_date (exact formula from the prompt). Removed the now-dead approvalRate from productionFlow() after confirming zero other callers via grep. Tile's icon swapped Activity -> XCircle (Activity had no other use in the file, removed from imports), danger-colored to match Fall-off Rate's red framing. ### 2026-07-31 (CC) — Prompt 396 shipped (URGENT security fix): Performance's Team toggle + Leaderboard were silently broken for every non-admin account

Brayden caught this live: Performance -> Team toggle and Leaderboard looked correct on his own admin account (showed Jordan's deal, Jordan in 1st) but he suspected it only worked because admin bypasses RLS. Confirmed directly against `can_view_agent()`'s own definition (migration 072): a closer can only see `policies` rows where `agent_id = auth.uid()`, their own downline (every real closer has none today), or admin. So every real agent's Team toggle and Leaderboard were silently collapsing to just their own single row - the client-side code in `Performance.jsx` was querying `policies` straight through `usePolicies(null)` and trusting RLS to hand back "the team," which only ever worked for the one account that bypasses RLS entirely.

Root rule going in: do NOT loosen `policies_select` broadly to fix this - that would let any agent read every other agent's `client_first_name`/`client_last_name`/`client_phone`/`policy_number`, recreating [[Prompt 379]]'s admin-only leak but company-wide instead. Built a narrow SECURITY DEFINER RPC instead: migration 093's `team_performance_policies()` returns only the non-PII fields Production's Team scope and the Leaderboard actually aggregate (`agent_id`, agent full_name via a `profiles` join, `policy_sold_date`, `effective_date`, `monthly_premium`, `annual_premium`, `status`, `cancellation_status`, `cancellation_call_at`, `created_at`) - no client name, phone, policy number, carrier, product, or notes. Granted to `authenticated` only, `anon`/`public` explicitly revoked - same grant pattern as `can_view_agent`/`downline_of` (migration 074). Added `useTeamPerformancePolicies()` to `usePolicies.js`; `Performance.jsx`'s `ProductionTab` now fetches "You" from the existing `usePolicies(null)` (unchanged, already correctly scoped to the account's own rows) and "Team" from the new RPC, and `LeaderboardTab` reads entirely from the RPC (its `p.agent?.full_name` join reference became `p.agent_name` to match the RPC's flat shape). Test-account exclusion (`testagent11`/nate44) stays client-side via the existing `excludeTestAccounts()`, unchanged.

**Applied the migration live** against `jjextitmbptoaolacocs` - asked Brayden directly in chat first (`AskUserQuestion`, same DDL-approval pattern as [[Prompt 392]]) since this is exactly the kind of live-DB schema change my own safety rules flag as needing explicit confirmation before acting; he approved, and it landed clean on the first try (no partial-execution retry needed, unlike 392's first attempt).

**Verified server-side, which is what actually matters here:** impersonated real closer account "nate hester" (`b6faff5d-63ab-46d7-a76b-4235879ab15d`) via `select set_config('request.jwt.claims', ...)` + `set local role authenticated` inside a rolled-back transaction against the live DB - raw `select count(*) from policies` returned **0** (proving the bug was real, not theoretical), then `select count(*) from team_performance_policies()` returned **20** (every company-wide policy row, proving the fix works). Separately confirmed `set local role anon; select team_performance_policies()` throws `permission denied for function team_performance_policies` - the RPC is authenticated-only as designed. `npx vite build` clean; `eslint` showed the same 4 pre-existing errors as `git stash` confirmed exist on `master` already (unused-var warnings in `usePolicies.js`/`Performance.jsx`, none on lines this prompt touched).

**Could NOT do the UI-level verification the prompt explicitly asked for** (log in as Armando/nate hester/Jordan and eyeball the actual Team toggle + Leaderboard) - same standing wall as every UI prompt this stretch: entering a password into any login form is a hard-blocked action under my own safety rules (not just the app's own classifier), so CC cannot get past the dev login screen for any account. ### 2026-07-31 (CC) — Prompt 399 shipped: underwriting banner aligned to effectuation banner, Yes/No locked to submitting agent

Two-part correction to [[Prompt 369]]'s underwriting banner. Shipped 0b98b23 on ohvara-dashboard, no migration.

**Alignment root cause:** `UnderwritingRow` had its own 2-column grid (`1fr max-content`) while `EffectuationRow` used a 3-column grid (`1fr max-content 260px`, the third column being the carrier-portal link) - since CSS grid's `max-content` button-column width is computed per-instance from that row's own content, missing the third column let the buttons sit further right on underwriting than effectuation. Fix: `UnderwritingRow` now shares `EFFECTUATION_GRID` and gained the identical portal-link column (reusing the existing `carrierPortalUrl()` lookup from [[Prompt 358]] Carrier Portals). Renamed the old `UNDERWRITING_GRID` constant to `NO_PORTAL_GRID` since `LapseCheckRow` (out of scope, untouched) is now its only user.

**Ownership lock:** added a `canAnswer`/`isOwner` check (`policy.agent_id === profile?.id`) to both banner types, in both places they render - the `MyPolicies.jsx` list row AND `PolicyModal.jsx`'s detail view (opened by clicking a row). The modal was the less obvious half of this bug: its `needsEffectuation`/`needsUnderwriting` were gated on the `canEdit` prop passed in from `MyPolicies.jsx` as `isAdmin || selected.agent_id === profile?.id` - meaning any admin viewing any policy in "Everyone" scope could already answer Yes/No there even before this prompt, same loophole as the list row. Deliberately did NOT reuse `canEdit` for the new lock (would've kept the same bug) - added a separate `isOwner` derived from a fresh `useAuth()` call in the modal instead, leaving `canEdit` exactly as-is for the status/cancellation dropdowns and delete button it legitimately still gates. Chose disabled+dimmed (opacity 0.45, tooltip "Only the submitting agent can answer this") over hidden for non-owners, specifically so the button column's width stays identical row-to-row - hiding would have reintroduced a version of the same alignment bug this prompt was fixing.

**Flagged as a known gap, not fixed:** this is UI-layer only. `policies_update`'s RLS (migration 072) is still `agent_id = auth.uid() or public.is_admin()` for the whole table, so a direct API call from an admin session could still technically flip these fields - closing that would need a column-aware trigger distinguishing "Yes/No click" from "admin's legitimate status-dropdown edit" on the same table, which is a meaningfully bigger lift than this prompt asked for. Different situation from [[Prompt 400]], where `team_messages_delete` was a single-purpose policy that could just be narrowed outright. Wrote this into LIVE_STATE's Prompt 399 entry rather than silently shipping a UI-only fix as if it were the full ask.

`npx vite build` clean. `eslint` on `PolicyModal.jsx` clean; `MyPolicies.jsx` shows one pre-existing `Date.now()`-in-`useMemo` react-hooks/purity error on line 100, confirmed via `git stash` to exist on `master` before this change - not introduced here.

### 2026-07-31 (CC) — Prompt 401 shipped: New Submission form data-quality fixes (phone mask, name title-case, required-field validation, approval dropdown unselected); queue empty again except Prompt 393 (HOLD)

New session, new queue item Eagle added since the last one. Shipped dbc728c on ohvara-dashboard, no migration - all four fixes from Brayden watching real submissions come through.

**Phone mask + title-case:** two new pure helpers in `lib/policyFormat.js` - `formatPhoneInput()` strips non-digits from the field's live value (including its own punctuation, so backspace/paste re-derive cleanly) and rebuilds `(xxx) xxx-xxxx` as digits accumulate; `titleCase()` runs once on submit, not while typing. Since CC can't get past the login screen to type into the actual field (same standing password-entry wall as every UI prompt, and this one specifically needed live interaction, not just a static screenshot), unit-tested both functions directly in Node outside the browser against partial lengths, over-10-digit input, letters mixed into digits, apostrophes (`o'brien` -> `O'Brien`), and hyphens (`mary-jane` -> `Mary-Jane`) - all correct. Worth remembering as a pattern: when the interactive verification path is blocked, pure functions can still get real proof instead of just an eyeballed diff.

**Required-field validation:** added a `REQUIRED_FIELDS` list + `validate()` covering every field but the auto-computed Annual Premium. Gave `TextField`/`AnchoredSelectField` in `components/ui/ExportForm.jsx` a new opt-in `error` boolean prop for the red-border highlight - deliberately additive (undefined for every other caller app-wide, and per [[Prompt 388]] that's literally every dropdown in the app, so this had to not change default rendering anywhere else). A missing field's red border clears itself the moment the agent edits it, not just on the next submit attempt, by threading a `fieldErrors` Set through the existing `set()` helper.

**Approval dropdown default removed:** `BLANK.underwriting_decision` changed from `'immediate'` to `''`, now one of the required fields.

**The one flagged ambiguity, resolved via AskUserQuestion instead of guessed:** the prompt itself said not to silently decide whether Effective Date should be required for a policy still in underwriting. Checked `usePolicies.js` first rather than asking blind - confirmed `pendingUnderwriting()` never reads `effective_date` and `pendingEffectuation()` explicitly excludes `pending_underwriting` rows, meaning the app's own logic already treats those two states as mutually exclusive. Took that finding to Brayden as a concrete tradeoff rather than an open question; his call was Effective Date required only when Approved is picked. Implemented as a separate check in `validate()`, not added to `REQUIRED_FIELDS`, so a still-in-underwriting submission with no effective date yet isn't blocked.
